title: DS grammar
preamble:
# DS grammar

The grammar of DS source files: lexical
structure (tokens, whitespace, comments, indentation handling),
syntactic structure (productions), and operator precedence.

This document is authoritative for DS syntax. If it
disagrees with any other language doc on a syntactic point,
this doc wins.

Paired with [LLEX], which describes how source
bytes become the terminal stream the productions consume. This
doc carries both the BNF productions and the prose rationale /
disambiguation notes — when normative grammar and prose
disagree, the productions in this doc win.

These productions are the specification, and a parser conforms
to them. When a parser and this document disagree, the parser
is wrong — including the reference one. A change to the
language is made here first, and the parser follows.

This doc does not specify semantics — those live in the
per-topic language specs (FACT_MODEL, EXPRESSIONS, etc.).
This doc specifies what a DS file *looks like* and how a
parser recognises its structure.

## What this is not

- Not a semantic specification. Behaviour of constructs
  (what `emit` does, what `logical` maintenance means, how
  `cooldown` enforces rate limits) lives in topical spec
  docs.
- Not an implementation guide. The reference compiler
  implements this grammar; compiler-internal choices
  (tokeniser structure, parser technique) are runtime
  concerns.
- Not exhaustive of every error condition. Individual
  constructs have their own compile-time diagnostics
  specified in their respective spec docs.
